subject: Data governance Q&A — residency, retention & deletion evidence for SOC 2/ISO
messages:
From: Aisha Reynolds <aisha.reynolds@financiatech.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: security@financiatech.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 16:14:00 +0000
Subject: Evidence request: residency, retention, deletion controls (SOC 2 / ISO audit)

Hi Neha,

Our external auditors for FinanciaTech are preparing for a SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 scope review and have requested evidence around data residency, retention schedules, and deletion controls for the workloads you host for us. We need the following artifacts to satisfy their checklist: 

- Formal data residency policy and configured regions for customer data (where applicable)
- Retention schedule / retention matrix that maps data classes to retention periods and legal basis
- Evidence of deletion workflows for customer-initiated deletion requests (runbooks + sample audit log entries showing deletion completion)
- Backup retention and deletion policy for snapshots and archived data (how long, deletion proof)
- Mapping of your controls to SOC 2 CC6/ISO Annex A controls (high level)
- Any DPA / Data Processing Addendum you typically execute (or a pointer to the signed document).

Our timeline is aggressive: auditors expect artifact delivery in ~10 business days. Can you confirm who we should coordinate with and whether you can provide the artifacts or an access link? I9ve attached our evidence checklist (FinanciaTech-SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx).

Thanks,
Aisha Reynolds
Security Operations
FinanciaTech

Attachment: FinanciaTech-SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: Evidence request: residency, retention, deletion controls (SOC 2 / ISO audit)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the checklist and the heads-up — we can support this. Looping in Rafael (SE) and Monica (Legal) and Michael (Security) on the inbound request so we can assemble artifacts.

Quick questions so we scope correctly:
- Do auditors need tamper-evident deletion logs (signed/log-store with immutability) or are plain audit entries sufficient?
- Do you want proof for both online data and long-term backups/archives?

Proposed timeline: we will gather the retention matrix, deletion runbook, deletion audit sample, S3/region config screenshots, and a mapping doc to SOC2/ISO within 7 business days. If the auditors require signed DPA or stamp-of-approval from Legal first, we may need an extra 2 days.

I will send a consolidated package and a secure Drive link to the artifacts.

Best,

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai <michael_grant@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Evidence request: residency, retention, deletion controls (SOC 2 / ISO audit)

Hi all,

I can take the technical artifacts. Quick notes on where evidence will come from and limitations:

- Residency: We tag tenant data at provisioning and attach region metadata. Config lives in our control plane (Confluence page + config snapshots). We can provide an export of tenant-region mappings and screenshots of the provisioned region in the Console. (Confluence link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Tenant+Residency)

- Retention matrix: We maintain a retention matrix in the Security docs. I9ll export an editable matrix to include data class mappings.

- Deletion workflow: We have an automated "customer-deletion" job that runs asynchronously; deletion events are logged to deletion-audit.log in the audit S3 bucket. Sample log line (redacted) we can provide is below: 

  2025-06-15T12:03:02Z | tenant_id=ft-2321 | request_id=del-8b7f | actor=customer-portal | object=customer-record-9921 | action=delete_initiated | status=completed | deletion_method=logical_purge | checksum=sha256:xxxxx

- Backups/archives: Snapshots are retained in cold storage for 30 days by default for hosted customers; dedicated/private can vary by contract. For FinanciaTech we will confirm snapshot retention and provide backup deletion confirmation entries where available.

- Evidence storage: Exports will go into a secure Drive folder, and we can provide sample logs rather than full exports. For tamper-evidence: our audit S3 bucket is write-once via object lock for selected artifacts; not all logs are currently under Object Lock — we can supply an explanation and timeline for increasing coverage.

I9ll prepare the technical package and target a first pass by Fri, 4 Jul. If Legal needs to sign off on wording before we hand to the auditor, flag it here.

-Michael
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai

Team,

I reviewed the checklist. We should provide:

- Current Data Retention Policy (dated) and the retention matrix (showing classes and legal basis)
- Deletion runbook + 3 sample redacted audit log entries per tenant (to protect other customers)
- Confirmation of backup retention and deletion practices (and an explanation of restore/retention windows)
- A signed or draft DPA. I9ve attached a redlined DPA template indicating the clauses I9d like to propose. Legal suggests we explicitly state retention limits for hosted customers and note exceptions for legal hold.

I will prepare the DPA language this morning and circulate a draft to Neha/Michael for review.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Neha,

Received the package and the Drive link — thank you. A couple quick follow-ups from the auditor: 

1) For backup deletion proof, they want one sample deletion entry that shows the snapshot ID and timestamp when the snapshot was purged. Can you confirm when Michael will have that?
2) For the deletion-audit log lines you provided, could you include one line showing the pre-deletion object checksum (to demonstrate content hash before purge) — redacted is fine.

If you can provide those two items by tomorrow EOD our auditor will be able to complete the review. Please route any DocuSign links for the DPA to our procurement contact (procurement@financiatech.com).

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Thanks,
Aisha
Security Operations, FinanciaTech
